definitions.explanation: A shop that sells bread and baked goods, or a person who runs such a shop.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}、パン{屋|や}でパンを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought bread at the bakery in the morning.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しいパン{屋|や}ができた。
examples.english: A new bakery opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: このパン{屋|や}は{朝|あさ}{早|はや}くから{焼|や}きたてのパンを{出|だ}すので、いつも{行列|ぎょうれつ}ができている。
examples.english: This bakery serves freshly baked bread from early morning, so there is always a line.

notes:
パン{屋|や} is a shop that sells bread and baked goods, or the person who runs such a shop. Japanese bakeries typically display a wide selection of individual rolls and pastries on trays, and customers pick items with tongs before paying at the register.

PATTERN: Follows the common product + {屋|や} (shop/seller) pattern: {花屋|はなや} (florist), {本屋|ほんや} (bookshop), {魚屋|さかなや} (fish shop). The {屋|や} suffix can refer to either the shop or the person who runs it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- パン{屋|や}に{行|い}く: to go to the bakery
- パン{屋|や}で{買|か}う: to buy at the bakery
- パン{屋|や}を{開|ひら}く: to open a bakery
- {町|まち}のパン{屋|や}: the neighborhood bakery

SIMILAR TERMS:
- ベーカリー: bakery (from English, often used for upscale or chain shops)
- {菓子|かし}{屋|や}: confectionery shop (sweets and cakes, not bread)
- パン{工房|こうぼう}: bread workshop/artisan bakery
